title: Chat permissions of the organization
summary: Owners and maintainers choose on the JayV site, for each chat permission (run commands, write to Git, use the network), whether it is free, always on or blocked in the organization's projects. An always-on one comes switched on in every chat and a blocked one shows disabled in the chat's Permissions as "Blocked by <organization>"; the agent is never given a blocked one.
usage: On the site, open the organization, Permissions tab, and use the Chat permissions box: for run commands, write to Git and use the network pick Free (people switch it on when they want), Always on or Blocked, and save. Right below are the blocked specific commands, on the same screen. In the app, under Permissions beside the work mode (or Ctrl+K › Command permissions), an always-on permission shows switched on and locked as "Always on by <organization>" and applies to every message of the chat; a blocked one shows disabled as "Blocked by <organization>". Blocking run commands also removes the commands granted one by one; blocking Git removes every git command; blocking the network removes the ones that reach the network. If an agent asks for such a command, JayV does not ask you: the step says who blocks it. If two organizations of the project disagree, the blocked one wins. It applies to the whole organization and reaches the app at the next sync. In the palette (Ctrl+K), "<organization>: chat permissions (site)" opens the tab.
